articles.author: Matthew Gault
articles.summary: Some people spent the week leading up to the release of Grand Theft Auto VI replaying the old games. I, sicko that I am, spent it watching TV news coverage of the franchise from the past 20 years. Grand Theft Auto has been a staple of cable and broadcast TV news since at least the release of Grand Theft Auto III in 2001. I’ve been an adult for all of it; I’ve had a front row seat for two decades of moral panics, parental freakouts, and bizarre political theater. The games and the broader culture’s reaction to them have changed dramatically in that time. In 2001, newscasters worried GTA III was training an army of young men to kill. In 2026, The New York Times earnestly quoted Bell Hooks in its review of GTA VI. For mainstream news, GTA is the ur-video game. The open world that mirrors our own, the prevalence of sex and death, and the increasingly realistic simulations and graphics pointed towards the dream of what a video game could be. Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China on Thursday will be the first time that the leaders of the US, China and Russia have gathered for talks as a trio. The trilateral on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is striking, but it is not an achievement. The lack of a clear agenda is telling: the spectacle really is the substance. Mr Trump sees international affairs in terms of spheres of influence. articles.summary: President Trump said in a brief phone interview Thursday that he won't make a determination on his next step in the Iran war until the new year. "I am not rushing into any decision [on Iran]. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year," Trump told Axios from Air Force One, on his way back to the U.S. from China. Why it matters: The president's comments come as he faces heavy pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to unleash a decisive bombing campaign soon. Yes, but: Trump could change his mind at any moment. And he wouldn't telegraph plans for an imminent attack even if that's what he was intending to do. A day before the war began in February, Trump said he hadn't made a decision, when in fact he had already ordered strikes. Between the lines: Trump's stated timing could mean he's giving more time for the naval blockade and the economic pressure campaign to play out, as many of his advisers and leaders of Gulf countries are urging. Issue No. 693 Olivia Charles: The Flaming Hydra Interview Elon Green Olivia Charles: The Flaming Hydra Interview by Elon Green Life has been continuously eventful for Olivia Charles, ever since she seriously took up the drums as a teenager. A natural choice of instrument, given that her father, Darryl “Chili” Charles, was a drummer himself . She’d put on her favorite records and play along: paying close attention to Joe Escalante of the Vandals, Lucky Lehrer of Circle Jerks and Philip “Fish” Fisher of Fishbone, at first, and then veering into post-punk: Lol Tolhurst of the Cure and Siouxsie and the Banshees’s Kenny Morris. “Having pocket, and then having the emotionality of being able to explode or retract, if I need to, or really break it down to the studs and be bare-boned—since I lacked the fundamentals and the technicality—it was all about that,” she said recently.
